parameters.content:
## Setup needed

**Airtable** - base is already connected. Create three tables:

**Employees** - personalEmail (unique), fullName, workEmail, role, department, managerEmail, location, startDate, employmentType, taskCount, documentCount, folderUrl, itProvisioned (checkbox), status, createdAt, completedAt, lastActionType, lastActionReason, lastActionAt, dayOffset

**Onboarding Tasks** - taskKey (unique, format: email::task title), employeeEmail, title, owner, dueDate, status

**Onboarding Documents** - documentKey (unique, format: email::documentName), employeeEmail, documentName, status, requestedAt, receivedAt, fileUrl

**Google Sheets** - a file named "Onboarding Automation" with tabs: Onboarding Log, Daily Actions Log, Error Log. Connect a Google Sheets credential.

**Google Drive and Calendar** - choose the parent folder and the calendar in those steps, and the folder for uploaded documents in **Save Document To Drive**.

**HR assistant** - run **Load HR Policies (Run Manually)** once, and again after every n8n restart. The policies are only kept in memory.

**Intake form login** - the new hire form is HR-only. Create a Basic Auth credential and select it in **New Hire Intake Form**. The document upload form stays open for new hires, but only accepts emails already in the Employees table.

**Errors** - already wired: Settings > Error Workflow points at this workflow. Re-select it if you import a copy.

## Why the plan is split into rows

The plan step produces a list of tasks and a list of documents. Two side branches turn these into one Airtable row per task and one per document.

That's the whole point: you can't follow up on something you never recorded. A checklist inside an email can't be tracked - separate rows with owners and due dates can.

Both branches match rows by personal email, so they don't have to wait for the employee record to be created first.

## What the daily check sends

**Decide Action For Today** looks at everyone still onboarding (all outstanding documents are fetched in one go, so nobody is skipped):

1. **One email to the new hire, max.** Milestone days (7 days before, day 0, 3, 7, 30) get the milestone email, with any missing documents listed inside it. Other days, missing documents get a reminder.
2. **Remind IT** - runs alongside, in Slack. Missing documents never hold up the key card and system access chase.
3. **Mark complete** - 30 days in, all documents in, IT confirmed.

If no one is currently onboarding, the daily run simply stops.

## 1 · New hire form, check & plan

HR fills in the new hire form. If the personal email, shift manager or start date is missing, onboarding stops and HR is alerted - nobody gets half set up.

**Generate Onboarding Plan** decides everything: based on the role, it builds the task list and document list. To change what each hotel role needs, edit it here only.

## 2 · Set everything up

Creates a private Drive folder, the employee record, a Day 1 orientation in the calendar, a Slack message to IT and the shift manager, a welcome email to the new hire, then a log entry.

Each step is set to keep going if it fails - a failed calendar invite shouldn't stop the welcome email.

## 3 · Turn the plan into trackable rows

The task list and document list become one Airtable row each.

That's the whole point: you can't follow up on what you never recorded. A checklist in an email can't be tracked - task rows with owners and due dates can.

Documents already **received** are skipped, so resubmitting the form never resets them to outstanding. Both branches match by personal email, so they don't wait for the employee record.

## 4 · Document upload

A separate form for the new hire. They choose which document they're sending and upload it. The email is cleaned up (trimmed, lowercased) and **must match a new hire in the Employees table** - anything else is ignored and HR is told, so the form can't be used to drop files into Drive.

The file is saved to Google Drive, and the matching Airtable row changes to "received" with a link to the file. This is what stops the daily reminders.

## 5 · Daily check - makes sure nothing is forgotten

Runs every day at 8:00. All outstanding documents are fetched once, so every person still onboarding is checked.

1. **One email to the new hire, max** - milestone email on day -7, 0 (start day), 3, 7 and 30, with any missing documents listed inside it. On other days, a missing-documents reminder.
2. **Remind IT** - in Slack, alongside the email. Missing documents never block the key card and system access chase.
3. **Mark complete** - 30 days in, all documents in, IT confirmed.

**If no one is onboarding, the daily run simply stops.**

## 6 · HR assistant - answers only from company policy

An internal chat for the People Team - it runs inside n8n and is not public, so new-hire emails point people to the People Team instead. It answers policy questions using only the uploaded HR documents.

It's told never to answer from general knowledge. If the policy doesn't cover something, it says so and points to the People Team.

This matters: a confident wrong answer about notice periods, tips or rest breaks is a legal problem, not just a support issue.

## 7 · Load HR policies - run manually

Downloads the policy document, splits it into sections and prepares it so the HR assistant can search it.

**The policies are kept in memory only** and are lost when n8n restarts. Run this again after any restart or policy change, or the assistant will have nothing to search.

For real use, switch to a permanent database such as Supabase or Pinecone.

## 8 · If something breaks

This branch runs whenever a live run fails. It works because the workflow is its own error workflow (**Settings > Error Workflow = this workflow**). If you import or duplicate it, select the copy there again.

It sends a Slack alert with the failed step and a link, and logs it to the Error Log tab.

Only runs for live runs, not manual tests.
